title: Payment Methods and Financial Responsibility
seo_title: Grade 8 Payment Methods and Financial Responsibility Worksheets (TEKS 8.12E, 8.12F, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.12E identify and explain the advantages and disadvantages of different payment methods; 8.12F analyze situations to determine if they represent financially responsible decisions and identify the benefits of financial responsibility and the costs of financial irresponsibility
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.12E and 8.12F: payment methods, fees and interest, and financially responsible decisions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Pay on time, avoid high-cost debt and pay for needs first.
key_sub: An $800 TV at 24% for a year costs $992.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Cash: you spend only what you have, but it is hard to replace. Checks: slow and not accepted everywhere.
  • Debit cards use your own money; overdrafts bring fees. Credit cards are loans; they can build credit but charge interest.
  • Electronic payments are fast and keep records.
  • Financial responsibility means paying on time, avoiding high-cost debt, saving and paying for needs first.

Examples

Example

$800 on a card at 24% for a year

0.24 × 800 = $192

Answer: $992 total

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a credit card is free moneyIt is a loan with interest.
Ignoring feesLate and overdraft fees add up quickly.
Buying wants before needsPay for housing, food and bills first.

faq.a: Identify and explain the advantages and disadvantages of different payment methods.
Analyze situations to determine if they represent financially responsible decisions and identify the benefits of financial responsibility and the costs of financial irresponsibility.
Spending more than is in your account. Banks often charge a fee.

faq.q: Can a credit card help you?
faq.a: Yes, if you pay the full balance on time: it builds a good credit history.

sets.title: Advantages and disadvantages of payment methods

items.q: What is an advantage of a debit card?
c: It cannot be used at stores
It always builds credit
It has no daily limit
It takes money you already have, so you avoid debt
items.e: A debit card spends money in your account.

items.q: What is one disadvantage of paying with cash?
c: It always costs interest
It cannot be replaced if it is lost or stolen
It needs a credit check
It is accepted nowhere
items.e: Lost cash is usually gone for good.

items.q: What is an advantage of electronic payments, like paying with a phone app?
c: They can never be hacked
They never need an account
They are fast and keep a record
They earn interest
items.e: Electronic payments are quick and leave a record.

items.q: What is one advantage of paying with cash?
c: It earns interest
It is easy to replace if lost
It builds a credit history
You can only spend what you have
items.e: With cash you cannot overspend, but it is hard to replace if lost.

items.q: What is an advantage of a credit card used responsibly?
c: It uses money from your savings
It can build a positive credit history
It cannot be stolen
It never charges interest
items.e: Paying the full balance on time builds good credit.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of a debit card?
c: Overdraft fees if you spend more than your balance
It needs a co-signer
It cannot be used online
It charges interest every month
items.e: Spending past your balance can bring overdraft fees.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of paying by check?
c: It can take days to clear and some stores do not accept it
It builds debt
It charges interest
It cannot be tracked
items.e: Checks are slow and not accepted everywhere.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of a credit card?
c: It cannot be used online
It takes money from your checking account right away
High interest if the balance is not paid in full
It has no record

items.e: $1,000 × 0.2 = $200 interest. Total = $1,200, compared with $1,000 in cash.

Use the rent money

items.q: Which is a financially responsible decision?
c: Paying the full credit card balance every month
Paying only the minimum and buying more
Taking a payday loan for concert tickets
Skipping the electric bill to buy shoes
items.e: Paying in full avoids interest and builds good credit.

items.q: What is a benefit of financial responsibility?
c: More late fees
Never needing a job
Lower interest rates and less stress about money
Higher prices at stores
items.e: Good habits bring better rates and peace of mind.

items.q: Which should come first in a budget?
c: Eating out every day
New video games
Concert tickets
Needs like housing and food

items.q: Which is not financially responsible?
c: Using a credit card for things you cannot pay off
Saving part of each paycheck
Keeping an emergency fund
Comparing prices before buying
items.e: Charging what you cannot repay leads to debt and interest.

items.q: What is a cost of financial irresponsibility?
c: Lower interest rates
More savings
Late fees, high interest and a poor credit history
A higher credit score
items.e: Missed payments bring fees, interest and bad credit.

items.q: A TV costs $300 at a store. A rent-to-own plan charges $8 a week for 78 weeks. How much more does rent-to-own cost?
items.e: $8 × 78 = $624. That is $324 more than buying it.

items.q: Kai owes $1,700 on a credit card at 20% interest. Which plan costs him the least in interest?
c: Pay only the minimum each month
Keep using the card for new purchases
Skip payments for a few months
Pay the full balance as soon as he can
items.e: Every month a balance stays, interest grows. Paying it off fast costs the least.
